title: The Danger of Uncontrolled Change
paragraphs: Today we focus on understanding the necessity of immutable laws. Why is it necessary to have laws that you do not change? Uncontrolled change will destroy. So although we want change and long for things to change, that change can in many cases be destructive. Our focus today is therefore the danger of uncontrolled change. First, I would like to make a remark about change. The most predictable reality on Earth is change. If there is one thing you can predict, it is change. Secondly, change is inherent in creation.

Everything will change. God created everything in such a way that it undergoes change in a natural manner. Every plant, every animal, the weather, the seasons, your body, your relationships, everything changes naturally. That brings me to point four. Man is the only creature in creation that has the power to determine change. They can design what kind of change they want. That is a dangerous power. Animals act on instinct. People don't. People have the power to decide what needs to change.

That is why humans have what we call willpower. Willpower is a curse and a blessing. And the greatest gift and the most dangerous gift that God has ever given to man is the will. The will is the power to decide. Animals act on instinct. We act on intent. Willpower is intention. The consequence of this is that God has placed willpower in the hands of man. And that means that the future of the world lies in the hands of humanity. We can determine what the Earth looks like.

This entails a number of very serious problems. We can determine what nations will look like, what communities will look like, what cultures will look like. We can determine what is normal and what is not normal. We can determine what is right and what is wrong, what is correct and what is incorrect. All that power lies in our hands. We can choose to love God or to curse Him. We can choose to reject the truth or create our own truth. This is a mighty power, the will, that God has given us.

And because of that, change is in our hands. I would like to briefly address what I call 'man-imposed change'. We are using our will to bring about changes in the world at this moment, and all countries are experiencing these changes. First, there is political confusion; constitutional amendments are taking place all over the world. Social transitions, ideological reinventions, philosophical instability. We also experience moral manipulation by our countries. Fluctuations in values. Our values fluctuate.

We are no longer sure what is important to us. Religious conflicts, scientific inventions, we determine how to use them. Technological progress and, of course, economic interdependence. We call it globalization. That is a huge change that is taking place. I find the last one very dangerous: the redefinition of terms. We are redefining things. Even words. Words like 'marriage'. We want to redefine it. So this is the world we live in. And I wanted to briefly take you through what I call the era of change.

Humanity has undergone a number of changes. And I will go through them very quickly. Some of you who study history will recognize them. You have probably heard of the Renaissance. Then we have the age of reason, the postmodern era. We have another era that we define as the era of secularism. Then we have the scientific era, the Enlightenment, the era of the humanist society. And then we have a recent era that we call the era of the new normal. Whatever that may mean.

And then we have what I am going to define as the era in which we live now. And it is the great era. We live in the era of experiments. We experiment with everything. We are messing with economic formulas. We are experimenting with relationships. We are experimenting with politics. We are experimenting with education. We are experimenting with all kinds of different cultural entities. We are not sure what we want. This is a dangerous period. We are living in an experimental phase.

What are the consequences of uncontrolled change? Let me give you a quick reality check. We see changes primarily the collapse of governments, the rise of people's power, international and domestic terrorism, failing states, a global economic crisis affecting everyone, and mass unemployment everywhere. And of course, we have the mismanagement and the disgrace of top officials in every field, whether it concerns politics, business, priests, bishops, or top managers. There seems to be no trust left in leadership.

Then there is a change in the moral compass of our world. Things that we used to consider immoral are now becoming acceptable. Another problem we see is the collapse of sovereignty, whereby countries are no longer sovereign because they are controlled by entities such as the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund, or the United Nations, which impose restrictions, criteria, and conditions on countries to participate in the global whole. This means that sovereignty has effectively disappeared.

And that is why I say that we are dealing with a collapse of sovereignty. These are all changes we are in the midst of. And I want you to listen carefully to me, because if you are not aware of this, you will be dragged along by it and become a victim of it. Let's take a brief look at the consequences of these changes. First, distrust of authority. People no longer trust leaders.

Then we see liberalism creeping in, lawlessness, permissiveness, compromise, immorality, a revision of morality, a culture of death taking over countries, a culture of violence, devaluation of human life, generational disillusionment, and sexual and social confusion. These are the consequences of the changes we are facing in the world. And I want you and I to handle this intelligently. For we will only be able to solve a problem if we can analyze it. The apostle Paul said to the people of God, that is you.

He said: "Do not be ignorant of the schemes of Satan." In other words: study your enemy before you attack. Understand the enemy's equipment, his weapons, and how he fights. This is exactly why Goliath was defeated. Because he had not studied David's weapon. David understood his weapon. He knew and understood Goliath's equipment. And therefore David killed him. We must understand what is happening to know what to do.

Earlier in this series, I already mentioned that the most important tribe of Israel was a small tribe, Issachar. Issachar is a tribe you do n't hear much about when it comes to the tribes of Israel, but God said that they were the most effective. God told us why: because they understood the spirit of the times and knew what they had to do. Only two things. So if you hear me talking like that, you have to listen carefully. I am trying to help you understand the spirit of the times, so that we know what to do.

Jesus once told the Pharisees and scribes, when he was teaching them about the kingdom, something he would hopefully never say to me. He said: "You do not know when your visitation will take place." In other words, you can miss God's plan because you do not realize what is going on. I hope God will never say that to me. So this is the world we live in. And here is a quote to write down: the world cannot heal itself from this situation.

Albert Einstein said something I often repeat: "You cannot solve a problem at the same level at which it arose." Jesus said it like this: "A bitter tree cannot bear sweet fruit." In other words, an unjust person cannot become a just government leader. You cannot demand sweet water from a bitter spring. That means that if humans have created the problems, humans cannot solve them either. Do you understand? Therefore, to save the world, God could find no one in the world to save it.

Because God loved the world so much, he used no one in the world to save it. He sent someone from outside the world to Earth. The sign that Jesus does not come from the earth is therefore a sign that we cannot save ourselves. That brings me to point two. Doing nothing is not an option. The world is collapsing. Nations are falling apart. Societal structures are collapsing. And the problem is that we can't just let it happen, because we are right in the middle of it. That brings you to point three. Write this down.

You must never criticize what you allow. In other words, you can never change what you avoid. And you must never criticize what you complain about. And that is why point five is so important. You must become the answer to your own prayer to change the world. You no longer have to ask God to send someone to solve something. This is the moment in your life when God says: solve it yourself. Do something about it. Take action, because you are responsible for this mistake.

And therefore God says to us: I want you to transform your society by showing leadership with influence from the Kingdom. What a heavy burden I feel in my mind right now. For you are responsible for what you allow. So if we sit back and allow them to pass laws we disagree with, we can never criticize those laws. So don't come back after four years with the statement: "I do n't agree with it." You were quiet. Jesus said: "Go to the rooftops and shout out the truth."

You are not responsible for people's reactions, but you are responsible for telling the truth. That is point number seven. Write it down. You can make things happen, or you can let them happen. And that is where we stand in life now. You can let things happen and become a victim of them, or you can decide: I am going to make sure that what happens, happens. I am going to ensure that I have influence on the decisions that are made and the changes we experience. God did not wait until we asked Him to save us.

God set the process in motion. For God so loved the world that He sent. He did not care whether the world loved Him or not. I love the world. He says: I am going to be proactive. I am going to act. That is what we are called to do, my friend. We are called to act. We are called to ensure that things do not just happen. Look at this photo on the wall. Don't you think this photo is beautiful? If we want a new society, we will have to do a number of things. I think this photo is beautiful. That is me.

Little fish, little fish, little fish. Read the statement at the top. Read. If you want something in your life that you have never had, you will have to do something that you have never done. In other words, jump. You have to take a chance. You might miss the bowl, you know, but at least you did n't stay with those who ended up in the bowl. You cannot change the world by playing it safe. No, you cannot change the world by being afraid of criticism.

It is the men or women who have decided that criticism is encouragement who become dangerous people. If you are not afraid of opposition, if you are not afraid of criticism, you are dangerous. So take a chance and jump. And that is what this service does. We are jumping out of the cocoon of the churches and going to follow God's obedient command. Go into the world and make disciples of all nations. I want you to read his next statement, because if you leave the group, you can get into trouble with your own friends.

Some of you are already laughing. Out loud. Read it. Please read it along with me. Go. I am making changes in my life. And if you don't hear from me, then you are one of them. There are people you have to leave behind in the old cocoon. Give God a helping hand for change. If you want to bring about change, you must change your life, change your relationships, and change your perspective in order to have an impact on the world. I want you to make a statement and write it down, please.

Our current era is therefore, what do I call it? The era of experimentation. And that means that we implement changes without taking into account the consequences or even the reality of the truth. We are experimenting. Recently, in America, the Supreme Court was asked a few weeks ago to consider the issue of same-sex marriage. The justices of the Supreme Court had to deal with this and debated it for about a week. One of them said something interesting.

I heard him say this: "We shouldn't delve into matters we don't yet understand." He mentioned, for example, the consequences of a child growing up in a family with two men or two women as husband and wife. He said that we do not even know the psychological impact on the child. What he is actually saying is that we are experimenting with the lives of children. It is scandalous to legally enshrine something whose consequences you do not yet know.

That is why I find it unfair that people in society make demands for the legalization of matters they have not investigated themselves. And that they expect you to approve it as an experiment. That is the era in which we live. An era of experimentation. I am looking at this board. This is how humans are. This sign describes man at this moment. People, look at those signs. Read those words aloud. Lost, confused, uncertain, unclear, bewildered, disoriented, stunned. That is us humans.
